claude-help.txt:
Usage: claude [options] [command] [prompt]

Claude Code - starts an interactive session by default, use -p/--print for
non-interactive output

Arguments:
  prompt                                Your prompt

Options:
  --add-dir <directories...>            Additional directories to allow tool
                                        access to
  --agent <agent>                       Agent for the current session. Overrides
                                        the 'agent' setting.
  --agents <json-or-file>               JSON object defining custom agents, or
                                        with --print the path to a file that
                                        holds one (e.g. '{"reviewer":
                                        {"description": "Reviews code",
                                        "prompt": "You are a code reviewer"}}')
  --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions  Enable bypassing all permission checks
                                        as an option, without it being enabled
                                        by default. Recommended only for
                                        sandboxes with no internet access.
  --allowedTools, --allowed-tools <tools...>
      Comma or space-separated list of tool names to allow (e.g. "Bash(git *)
      Edit")
  --append-system-prompt <prompt>       Append a system prompt to the default
                                        system prompt
  --autocompact <auto|tokens>           Auto-compact window size (auto, or
                                        100k–1M tokens)
  --ax-screen-reader                    Render screen-reader friendly output
                                        (flat text, no decorative borders or
                                        animations).
  --bg, --background                    Start the session in the background and
                                        return immediately. Prints the id that
                                        `claude attach`, `logs`, `stop` and `rm`
                                        take; `claude agents` lists them. With
                                        --resume <session-id>, continues that
                                        session in the background under the same
                                        ID, or starts a copy and says so when
                                        the session is already running
  --bare                                Minimal mode: skip hooks (those defined
                                        in settings and by installed plugins;
                                        features built into Claude Code are
                                        unaffected), LSP, plugin sync,
                                        attribution, auto-memory, background
                                        prefetches, keychain reads, and
                                        CLAUDE.md auto-discovery. Sets
                                        CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1. Anthropic auth is
                                        strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or
                                        apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and
                                        keychain are never read). 3P providers
                                        (Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry) use their own
                                        credentials. Skills still resolve via
                                        /skill-name. Explicitly provide context
                                        via: --system-prompt[-file],
                                        --append-system-prompt[-file], --add-dir
                                        (CLAUDE.md dirs), --mcp-config,
                                        --settings, --agents, --plugin-dir.
  --betas <betas...>                    Beta headers to include in API requests
                                        (API key users only)
  --brief                               Enable SendUserMessage tool for
                                        agent-to-user communication
  --chrome                              Enable Claude in Chrome integration
  --cloud [description|session_id|url]  Create a cloud session with the given
                                        description, or attach to an existing
                                        one by session ID or claude.ai/code URL
  -c, --continue                        Continue the most recent conversation in
                                        the current directory
  --dangerously-skip-permissions        Bypass all permission checks.
                                        Recommended only for sandboxes with no
                                        internet access.
  -d, --debug [filter]                  Enable debug mode with optional category
                                        filtering (e.g., "api,hooks" or
                                        "!1p,!file")
  --debug-file <path>                   Write debug logs to a specific file path
                                        (implicitly enables debug mode)
  --desktop                             Open in the Claude Desktop app instead
                                        of the terminal (with --continue or
                                        --resume <id> to pick the session)
  --disable-slash-commands              Disable all skills
  --disallowedTools, --disallowed-tools <tools...>
      Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny (e.g. "Bash(git *)
      Edit")
  --effort <level>                      Effort level for the current session
                                        (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)
  --environment <environment_id>        Create a new cloud session that runs on
                                        the given self-hosted environment
                                        (ccpool_...).
  --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
      Move per-machine sections (cwd, env info, memory paths, git status) from
      the system prompt into the first user message. Improves cross-user
      prompt-cache reuse. Only applies with the default system prompt (ignored
      with --system-prompt). (default: false)
  --fallback-model <model>              Enable automatic fallback to specified
                                        model(s) when the default model is
                                        overloaded or not available. Accepts a
                                        comma-separated list to try each in
                                        order. Re-tries the primary at the start
                                        of each user turn.
  --file <specs...>                     File resources to download at startup.
                                        Format: file_id:relative_path (e.g.,
                                        --file file_abc:doc.txt
                                        file_def:img.png)
  --fork-session                        When resuming, create a new session ID
                                        instead of reusing the original (use
                                        with --resume or --continue)
  --forward-subagent-text               Forward subagent text and thinking
                                        blocks as assistant/user messages with
                                        parent_tool_use_id set (only works with
                                        --print and --output-format=stream-json)
  --from-pr [value]                     Resume a session linked to a PR by PR
                                        number/URL, or open interactive picker
                                        with optional search term
  -h, --help                            Display help for command
  --ide                                 Automatically connect to IDE on startup
                                        if exactly one valid IDE is available
  --include-hook-events                 Include all hook lifecycle events in the
                                        output stream (only works with
                                        --output-format=stream-json)
  --include-partial-messages            Include partial message chunks as they
                                        arrive (only works with --print and
                                        --output-format=stream-json)
  --input-format <format>               Input format (only works with --print):
                                        "text" (default), or "stream-json"
                                        (realtime streaming input) (choices:
                                        "text", "stream-json")
  --json-schema <schema>                JSON Schema for structured output
                                        validation. Example:
                                        {"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}
  --max-budget-usd <amount>             Maximum dollar amount to spend on API
                                        calls (only works with --print)
  --mcp-config <configs...>             Load MCP servers from JSON files or
                                        strings (space-separated)
  --model <model>                       Model for the current session. Provide
                                        an alias for the latest model (e.g.
                                        'fable', 'opus', or 'sonnet') or a
                                        model's full name.
  -n, --name <name>                     Set a display name for this session
                                        (shown in the prompt box, /resume
                                        picker, and terminal title)
  --no-chrome                           Disable Claude in Chrome integration
  --no-session-persistence              Disable session persistence - sessions
                                        will not be saved to disk and cannot be
                                        resumed (only works with --print)
  --output-format <format>              Output format (only works with --print):
                                        "text" (default), "json" (single
                                        result), or "stream-json" (realtime
                                        streaming) (choices: "text", "json",
                                        "stream-json")
  --permission-mode <mode>              Permission mode to use for the session
                                        (choices: "acceptEdits", "auto",
                                        "bypassPermissions", "manual",
                                        "dontAsk", "plan")
  --permission-prompts <target>         Who answers permission prompts with
                                        --print: "host" (the SDK host or
                                        --permission-prompt-tool) or "none"
                                        (nobody: anything that would prompt is
                                        denied automatically; the permission
                                        mode still decides everything else)
                                        (choices: "host", "none", default:
                                        "host")
  --plugin-dir <path>                   Load a plugin from a directory or .zip
                                        for this session only; a folder of
                                        plugins loads each child (repeatable:
                                        --plugin-dir A --plugin-dir B.zip)
                                        (default: [])
  --plugin-url <url>                    Fetch a plugin .zip from a URL for this
                                        session only (repeatable: --plugin-url A
                                        --plugin-url B) (default: [])
  -p, --print                           Print response and exit (useful for
                                        pipes). Note: The workspace trust dialog
                                        is skipped when Claude is run in
                                        non-interactive mode (via -p, or when
                                        stdout is not a TTY, e.g. piped or
                                        redirected output). Only use this in
                                        directories you trust. Settings files
                                        that fail validation are silently
                                        ignored in this mode (no error dialog is
                                        shown).
  --prompt-suggestions [value]          Enable prompt suggestions. In print/SDK
                                        mode, emits a prompt_suggestion message
                                        after each turn with a predicted next
                                        user prompt (choices: "true", "false",
                                        "1", "0", "yes", "no", "on", "off",
                                        preset: "true")
  --remote-control [name]               Start an interactive session with Remote
                                        Control enabled (optionally named)
  --remote-control-session-name-prefix <prefix>
      Prefix for auto-generated Remote Control session names (default: hostname)
  --replay-user-messages                Re-emit user messages from stdin back on
                                        stdout for acknowledgment (only works
                                        with --input-format=stream-json and
                                        --output-format=stream-json)
  --restricted                          Restricted mode: removes the built-in
                                        tools that run commands or code (Bash,
                                        PowerShell and the other code-running
                                        tools) and WebFetch unless --tools names
                                        them, and ignores user, project and
                                        local settings files (managed settings
                                        and --settings still apply; add
                                        --strict-mcp-config to skip MCP servers
                                        too). Also confines the file tools to
                                        the working directories (--add-dir
                                        included), refuses bypassPermissions,
                                        and lets only a person or the configured
                                        permission handler approve writes to
                                        settings, git and tool-configuration
                                        files.
  -r, --resume [value]                  Resume a conversation by session ID, or
                                        open interactive picker with optional
                                        search term
  --safe-mode                           Start with all customizations
                                        (CLAUDE.md, skills, installed plugins,
                                        hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and
                                        agents, output styles, workflows, custom
                                        themes, keybindings, and more) disabled
                                        — useful for troubleshooting a broken
                                        configuration. Admin-managed (policy)
                                        settings still apply. Auth, model
                                        selection, built-in tools and plugins,
                                        and permissions work normally. Sets
                                        CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE=1.
  --session-id <uuid>                   Use a specific session ID for the
                                        conversation (must be a valid UUID)
  --setting-sources <sources>           Comma-separated list of setting sources
                                        to load (user, project, local).
  --settings <file-or-json>             Path to a settings JSON file or a JSON
                                        string to load additional settings from
  --strict-mcp-config                   Only use MCP servers from --mcp-config,
                                        ignoring all other MCP configurations
  --system-prompt <prompt>              System prompt to use for the session
  --system-prompt-snapshot <on|off>     Record the system prompt once per
                                        conversation and reuse it verbatim on
                                        every request and resume. on (the
                                        default): the prompt is rendered on the
                                        conversation's first request — a
                                        --system-prompt or
                                        --append-system-prompt included — sent,
                                        and recorded; every later request and
                                        resume sends the record as-is, even when
                                        a later launch passes different text,
                                        until the conversation is compacted.
                                        off: never record; the prompt is
                                        rendered fresh every request (for
                                        iterating on prompt text). No effect
                                        where system-prompt recording is not yet
                                        enabled. (choices: "on", "off")
  --teleport [session]                  Resume a teleport session, optionally
                                        specify session ID
  --tmux                                Create a tmux session for the worktree
                                        (requires --worktree). Uses iTerm2
                                        native panes when available; use
                                        --tmux=classic for traditional tmux.
  --tools <tools...>                    Specify the list of available tools from
                                        the built-in set. Use "" to disable all
                                        tools, "default" to use all tools, or
                                        specify tool names (e.g.
                                        "Bash,Edit,Read").

gh-pr-diff-help.txt:
View changes in a pull request.

Without an argument, the pull request that belongs to the current branch
is selected.

With `--web` flag, open the pull request diff in a web browser instead.

Use `--exclude` to filter out files matching a glob pattern. The pattern
uses forward slashes as path separators on all platforms. You can repeat
the flag to exclude multiple patterns.

By default, terminal escape sequences in the diff are neutralized, since
they could manipulate your terminal. Pass `--allow-escape-sequences` to
print the diff verbatim, for example when piping a patch to another program.


USAGE
  gh pr diff [<number> | <url> | <branch>] [flags]

FLAGS
      --allow-escape-sequences   Allow printing terminal escape sequences
      --color string             Use color in diff output: {always|never|auto} (default "auto")
  -e, --exclude patterns         Exclude files matching glob patterns from the diff
      --name-only                Display only names of changed files
      --patch                    Display diff in patch format
  -w, --web                      Open the pull request diff in the browser

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # See diff for current branch
  $ gh pr diff
  
  # See diff for a specific PR
  $ gh pr diff 123
  
  # Exclude files from diff output
  $ gh pr diff --exclude '*.yml' --exclude 'generated/*'
  
  # Exclude matching files by name
  $ gh pr diff --name-only --exclude '*.generated.*'

rup-help.txt:
rup: the command line of roundup

roundup runs coding Agents in a Project and shows the user their Status, Todos, Pads, Messages and Terminals. rup is how an Agent reads and changes all of that from its shell: every command acts as you, the Agent whose id is in ROUNDUP_AGENT.

Human-readable command output names Agents by Rail name. IDs remain command arguments and machine fields in --json.

Examples:
  rup pad read notes
  rup terminal read 3 --after 120
  rup todo create "Fix login"
  rup pad write notes - < notes.md

Commands:

  terminal
    rup terminal open [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--workstream <workstream>]
        Start a login shell in a Terminal owned by a Workstream that is yours or in your Reach; `workstream` is required for Agents.
    rup terminal spawn <cwd> <cols> <rows> [--command <command>]... --env <env>
        Start a program in a Terminal owned by you; the answer holds its `id`.
    rup terminal close <id>
        Stop a Terminal you or your Reach own and forget it.
    rup terminal write <id> [<text>] [--no-enter] [--base64 <base64>]
        Type text into a Terminal you or your Reach own, then press Enter.
    rup terminal resize <id> <cols> <rows>
        Resize a Terminal you or your Reach own to `cols` by `rows`.
    rup terminal kill <id>
        Stop the program of a Terminal you or your Reach own.
    rup terminal show <id>
        Show a Terminal in your Reach to the user, who sees its owner selected. [Door only]
    rup terminal screen <id>
        Read a Terminal's screen as it is now, as plain text, with the `offset` to read from next.
    rup terminal read <id> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Read a Terminal's output you have not read yet, as plain text; `next` is the offset after it.
    rup terminal search <id> <pattern> [--after <after>] [--max <max>]
        Search a Terminal's output for a regular expression and get the matching lines with their offsets.

  agent
    rup agent spawn <cwd> [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--engine <engine>] [--prompt <prompt>] [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>] [--name <name>] [--model <model>] [--scout] [--specialist <specialist>] [--extras <extras>]
        Start a child Agent in a folder of this Project.
    rup agent extras
        List the skills, plugins and MCP servers of the user's setup that `agent_spawn`'s `extras` and `agent_extras_add` accept. [Door only]
    rup agent extras-add <id> --extras <extras>
        Give a running child of yours skills, plugins or MCP servers by name. [Door only]
    rup agent stop <id>
        Stop an Agent in your Reach, never yourself.
    rup agent prompt <id> <text>
        Send a prompt to an Agent in your Reach as the user would.
    rup agent interrupt <id>
        Interrupt the turn of an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent worktree-state <id>
        Read what a Worktree holds: its changes and whether it can land.
    rup agent land <id>
        Land the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach on the Base branch.
    rup agent discard <id>
        Discard the Worktree of an Agent in your Reach and its changes.
    rup agent set-order [--captured <captured>] --order <order>
        Replace your own order: a Work order once the ask is clear, or a Clarification order while a question is open.
    rup agent instructions <id>
        Read exact instruction revisions and Attempt-bound delivery facts for yourself or an Agent in your Reach.
    rup agent run [--cols <cols>] [--rows <rows>] [--cwd <cwd>] --command <command>...
        Run a command in a Terminal of your own that the user can watch, in your Worktree or in `cwd`.
    rup agent resume <id> [--mode <normal>]
        Continue a saved conversation in your Reach.
    rup agent context
        Ask where you stand now: whom you report to, whom to ask, your peers, your open Todos and the Models you may start a child on.
    rup agent digest
        Ask what each of your direct children did: its Kind, its last line, its open Todos and the Pads it wrote since you were last told. [Door only]
    rup agent wake <id>... [--any]
        Ask to be woken when all, or with `any` the first, of the named Agents finish (idle, done, error or needs-you).

  rail
    rup rail tree
        Read the Rail: every Workstream, Agent and Terminal with its Status.
    rup rail create-workstream <name> [--parent <parent>] [--order <order>]
        Make a Workstream at the Project root, with `parent` null.
    rup rail move <id> <index> [--parent <parent>]
        Move a node in your Reach: an Agent under a Workstream or Agent, a Workstream only to the root.
    rup rail rename <id> <name>
        Rename yourself or a node in your Reach.
    rup rail start-door <id>
        Start the Door of a Workstream you made, or of one in your Reach.
    rup rail remove <id> [--scope <this>] [--operation <operation>]
        Remove a node in your Reach, never yourself.

  project
    rup project set-worktrees --on [--check <check>]
        Turn Worktrees on or off for the Project and set the command Landing runs.
    rup project get
        Read the Project's settings.
    rup project open <path>
        Ask the App to open the Project at an absolute folder path.
    rup project rename <name>
        Ask the App to give this Project a name of 1 to 40 characters.

  import
    rup import list <period>
        Read-only: list this Project's saved and live top-level Claude Code sessions active in the period, once each, with the revision to approve.

  todo
    rup todo create <title> [--body <body>] [--blockers <blockers>]... [--owner <owner>] [--priority <low>]
        Create a Todo.
    rup todo get <id>
        Read one Todo.
    rup todo list
        List every Todo.
    rup todo update <id> [--title <title>] [--body <body>] [--priority <low>] [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Change a Todo's title, body or priority.
    rup todo complete <id>
        Mark a Todo done.
    rup todo reopen <id>
        Reopen a done Todo.
    rup todo set-blockers <id> --blockers <blockers>... [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Replace a Todo's whole blocker list.
    rup todo assign <id> [--owner <owner>] [--expected-change <expected_change>]
        Assign a Todo to an owner, or leave it unassigned.
    rup todo move <id> [--home <home>]
        Move a Todo into a Workstream, or out of every Workstream with a null `home`.
    rup todo reorder <id> [--before <before>]
        Put a Todo before another in the Todo order, or last with a null `before`.
    rup todo delete <operation> --ids <ids>...
        Delete exactly the chosen Todo ids.
    rup todo comment <id> <body>
        Leave a comment on a Todo only when the user must read it, such as a question or a blocker.
    rup todo comments <id>
        Read a Todo comment thread oldest first, including authors and user replies.
    rup todo ref add <id> <url>
        Point the user to a Pad or one section of it from a Todo, so they open it from the Todo and read it.
    rup todo ref remove <id> <url>
        Remove a Pad or Pad-section link from a Todo, by the same link you added; removing one the Todo lacks changes nothing.

  pad
    rup pad create <name> [--text <text>]
        Create a shared Pad.
    rup pad read <name>
        Read one Pad.
    rup pad list
        List every Pad.
    rup pad rename <name> <new-name> <expected-incarnation>
        Rename any Pad, keeping its creation and text.
    rup pad write <name> <text> [--expected-revision <expectedRevision>] [--expected-incarnation <expectedIncarnation>]
        Rewrite a Pad's whole text.
    rup pad append <name> <text>
        Add text to the end of any Pad.
    rup pad append-section <name> <heading> <text> [--expected-revision <expectedRevision>]
        Add text at the end of the section under a Markdown heading of any Pad; the heading ignores case and extra whitespace.
    rup pad move <name> [--home <home>]
        Move a Pad to a Workstream or the Project root.
    rup pad delete <name> [--operation <operation>] [--expected-incarnation <expectedIncarnation>]
        Delete a Pad, retaining its original creation for restoration.
    rup pad redo-delete <project> <restored-operation> <operation> <expected-incarnation> <expected-revision> [--expected-home <expectedHome>]
        Redo a restored Pad deletion with an acknowledged creation, Revision and Home; retain the current authoritative state for Undo.
    rup pad get-deletion <operation>
        Reconcile an unknown Pad deletion on its originating Project.
    rup pad restore <project> <operation>
        Restore your retained Pad deletion once, without replaying external effects.
    rup pad export <name> <path>
        Write a Pad's text to a file at an absolute path.
    rup pad set-storage --files
        Choose whether the Project mirrors its Pads to files.

  message
    rup message send <to> <kind> <body> [--reply-to <replyTo>]
        Send a note or a question to an Agent or the user.
    rup message get <id>
        Read one Message you sent or received.
    rup message list [--to <to>] [--id <id>] [--status <pending>]
        List the Messages you sent or received, newest last.
    rup message progress <project> <id>
        Inspect retained instructions, reports, acceptance and declared verification without starting work.
    rup message report <project> <id> <key> <delivery> <result> <next> --target <target> --output <output> --state <state> --check <check>
        Report your own Attempt's result for an exact delivered instruction and published output.
    rup message accept-result <project> <id> <report> <evidence>
        Record user acceptance of one exact reported result with its evidence; only the user may accept.
    rup message verify-result <project> <id> <report>
        Observe a report's declared authoritative condition without a Model call; unavailable or unsupported evidence stays unknown.
    rup message resolve-result <project> <id> <report> <source>
        User only: authorize a read-only authoritative receipt source for an unknown external effect.
    rup message reconcile-work <project> <id>
        Read which retained work is unfinished, confirmed, pending a check or uncertain, without sending or starting anything.
    rup message resume-work <project> <id> <request> [--action <action>]
        User only: resume an Agent's eligible unfinished work with one successor Message.

  route
    rup route set <from> <to> <delivery>
        Set where one Agent's Messages to another go: `auto` or `drop`.
    rup route list
        List the Routes: who each Agent's questions go to.

  deliverable
    rup deliverable publish <key> <title> --target <target>
        Deliberately publish a file, expected Pad incarnation and Revision or current external URL.
    rup deliverable list [--home <home>] [--maker <maker>]
        List published results without reading retained payloads.
    rup deliverable get <project> <id>
        Read publication metadata by its Project and identity.
    rup deliverable resolve <project> <id>
        Resolve the recorded revision or exact current external target, or its unavailability cause.
    rup deliverable move <project> <id> [--home <home>]
        Move a published result; an Agent cannot override user placement.
    rup deliverable remove <project> <id>
        Explicitly remove a publication.

  github
    rup github pr-get <number>
        Read a PR of the Project's repository as GitHub holds it now: title, body, state, draft, autoMerge, head and mergedAt. [Door only]
    rup github issue-get <number>
        Read an Issue of the Project's repository as GitHub holds it now: title, body, state, labels and stateReason. [Door only]
    rup github pr-set-body <number> <body>
        Replace a PR's body with `body` (not empty); the answer is the PR as it now stands. [Door only]
    rup github pr-ready <number>
        Mark a draft PR ready for review; a PR already ready is left as it is. [Door only]
    rup github pr-auto-merge <number>
        Enable auto-merge (merge commit) on an open PR; one already enabled is left as it is. [Door only]

  api
    rup api list [--quiet]
        List every method the Daemon serves with a one-line summary.
    rup api describe <method>
        Describe one method: its summary, params and result schemas and an example.

  link
    rup link read <url>
        Read a Project roundup:// link: current Pad, Todo, Agent, Workstream or Terminal content, or a Deliverable recorded revision/current external target and its availability.

  provenance
    rup provenance history <item>
        List the Touches on one item, such as `todo:3` or `rail:5`.
    rup provenance touched <actor-id>
        List the Touches one Actor made.


  workstream
    rup workstream rewind --turns <turns>...
        Ask each named child's provider to rewind it through the provider's own feature: Claude Code restores the child's files to the state at the user message `turn` of its conversation. [Door only]

  streams
    rup events [--after <after>] [--follow]
        Print the Events saved after a number, one JSON object per line, then stop at the end of the log.
        Example: rup events --after 12 --follow --json

  actions
    rup actions [--json]
        List the App's named actions.
        Example: rup actions
    rup do <name> [key=value]...
        Run a named action of the App.
        Example: rup do agent.new-with-prompt prompt="Fix login"

  other
    rup help [<command>]
        Print this help, or a command's.
    rup ping
        Check the Daemon answers.
    rup mcp <agent-id>
        Serve these commands as MCP tools over stdio.
    rup signal <agent-id>
        Hook: hand the Daemon a Signal from stdin.
    rup context <agent-id>
        Hook: print the Agent's Context.
    rup skill <setup|status|remove>
        Teach other Claude Code sessions about roundup.

Options of every command:
    --agent <id>   Act as this Agent instead of ROUNDUP_AGENT
    --json         Print the result as JSON on stdout
    -h, --help     Print a command's arguments, flags and an example

A text argument takes `-` to read the whole of stdin, so a long body is never quoted.
`rup help <noun>` lists a noun's commands; `rup help <noun> <verb>` describes one.

Exit codes:
    0  done
    1  failed: the Daemon refused, did not answer within 10 s, or was not there
    2  bad usage: an unknown command, a missing or invalid argument, no Agent id, a Door-only command run by an Agent

rup drives rupd, the roundup Daemon, from a shell or an MCP client.

usage: rup [--as ext:<name>] [--json] <command>

commands, and who may run each (User: a shell outside every Agent; Ext: --as ext:<name>):
  ping        show which Daemon answered
              User: yes   Ext: yes
  mcp         serve the roundup tools over MCP on stdio (rup mcp <agent-id> for an Agent)
              User: yes   Ext: yes
  signal      an Agent's hook (rup signal <agent-id>)
              User: no    Ext: no
  context     an Agent's hook (rup context <agent-id>)
              User: no    Ext: no
  help        print this text

options, before the command:
  --as ext:<name>  act as the Ext Actor ext:<name> (1 to 64 of a-z 0-9 - _), so calls are Touches under that name
  --json           with ping, print {actor, socket, result}, who rup acted as included

RUPD_SOCKET names the Daemon's socket; unset, rup uses ~/.roundup/rupd.sock.
`rup ping` shows which Daemon answered.
rup-skill-help.txt:
rup skill: teach other Claude Code sessions about roundup

Usage:
    rup skill setup [--dry-run] [--force] [--json]
        Install roundup's skill and hook. Example: rup skill setup --dry-run
    rup skill status [--json]
        Say what is installed. Example: rup skill status --json
    rup skill remove [--dry-run] [--json]
        Take out only what setup installed. Example: rup skill remove
    rup skill report --state <state> [--kind <kind>] [--where]
        Internal: the hook's command. Writes one status report to the terminal and always exits 0.

Options:
    --dry-run   Print what would happen with each outcome prefixed `would `, and write nothing
    --force     Replace a skill named roundup that roundup did not install (setup only)
    --json      Print the list as one JSON document

Exit codes:
    0  done
    1  setup or remove met a foreign, unreadable or unsupported item, or a write failed
    2  bad usage
